title: Cylinders, Cones & Spheres
subtitle: Volume in Terms of π
bounds: PROTOCOL §4b π volumes. Radii 1-5 (a sphere's or hemisphere's only 1 or 3, or 2 in 'using 3 for π'), diameters 2-10 and even, heights 1-10. Every π coefficient is a whole number 1-100 reached through times-table steps in some order (2 × 5 × 5 is 10 × 5; 9 ÷ 3 × 4 is 3 × 4): each × has both factors 1-10, each ÷ divisor and quotient 2-10, every value 100 or less. Exceptions: (4/3)π and (2/3)π for a radius-1 sphere or hemisphere; halving a diameter (÷ 2, quotient 1-5); square roots of 4 and 9 and cube roots of 1 and 27. 'Using 3 for π' answers are whole numbers 1-100 (the 3 cancels the thirds). Scale questions use factors 2, 3 and 1/2 on a radius or height. Wrong choices up to 999.

tiers.name: Cylinders
tiers.description: Volume = base area × height: π × r × r × h. Square the radius.

tiers.name: Cones
tiers.description: A cone is one third of the cylinder with the same base and height.

tiers.name: Spheres
tiers.description: Sphere: (4/3) × π × r × r × r. A hemisphere is half of that.

tiers.name: Work Backward & Estimate
tiers.description: Find a height or radius from the volume. Use 3 for π.

tiers.name: Compare & Scale
tiers.description: Double a length and the volume changes by 2, 4 or 8 times.

NO_SQUARE.student: The radius is used twice: π × r × r. Multiply it by itself first.
NO_SQUARE.teacher: Uses r where r × r belongs (forgets to square the radius).

LATERAL_AREA.student: Doubling r is not squaring it. The base area is π × r × r.
LATERAL_AREA.teacher: Doubles the radius instead of squaring it (the 2πr of the edge).

FORGOT_HEIGHT.student: Volume stacks the base up the whole height. Multiply by the height.
FORGOT_HEIGHT.teacher: Gives the base area and leaves out the height.

ADDED_HEIGHT.student: Multiply the base area by the height. Do not add them.
ADDED_HEIGHT.teacher: Adds the height to the base instead of multiplying.

DIAMETER_AS_RADIUS.student: Halve the diameter first: the formula wants the radius.
DIAMETER_AS_RADIUS.teacher: Puts the diameter into the formula where the radius belongs.

HALVED_AFTER_SQUARE.student: Halve the diameter first, then square it. Not the other way.
HALVED_AFTER_SQUARE.teacher: Squares the diameter and then halves once (gets 2 × r × r).

AREA_AS_RADIUS.student: The base area is already the π part. Do not square it again.
AREA_AS_RADIUS.teacher: Treats the base area number as a radius and squares it.

FORMULA_MIX.student: Volume is base area times height: the layers stack up.
FORMULA_MIX.teacher: Names the wrong measure in the volume formula.

CIRCUMFERENCE_FOR_AREA.student: Around the edge is 2πr. The area inside is π × r × r.
CIRCUMFERENCE_FOR_AREA.teacher: Gives a circumference formula for the base area.

RADIUS_NOT_SQUARED.student: Area needs r twice: π × r × r, not just π × r.
RADIUS_NOT_SQUARED.teacher: Writes the circle area as π × r (one r).

SAME_BASE_SAME_VOLUME.student: Same base, but a taller cylinder stacks more layers.
SAME_BASE_SAME_VOLUME.teacher: Thinks equal bases mean equal volumes and ignores height.

SHORTER_HOLDS_MORE.student: Taller means more layers of the same base: more volume.

CANT_TELL.student: Same base area, so the height decides: taller holds more.
CANT_TELL.teacher: Thinks the heights are needed to compare.

NO_THIRD.student: A cone is only one third of its cylinder. Divide by 3.
NO_THIRD.teacher: Gives the cylinder's volume for the cone (no 1/3).

HALF_FOR_THIRD.student: A cone is one third of its cylinder, not one half.

TIMES_THREE.student: A cone is a third of the cylinder: divide by 3, do not multiply.

SAME_AS_CYLINDER.student: A cone is smaller than its cylinder: one third of it.
SAME_AS_CYLINDER.teacher: Says the cone and the cylinder hold the same.

SAME_AS_CONE.student: Three cones fill the cylinder, so it is 3 times the cone.
SAME_AS_CONE.teacher: Says the cylinder holds the same as the cone.

DIVIDED_BY_THREE.student: The cylinder is 3 times the cone: multiply by 3.
DIVIDED_BY_THREE.teacher: Divides by 3 where the cylinder needs 3 times the cone.

ADDED_THREE.student: Three cones fill the cylinder: multiply by 3, do not add 3.

NO_FOUR_THIRDS.student: A sphere is (4/3) × π × r × r × r. Keep the 4/3.
NO_FOUR_THIRDS.teacher: Leaves the 4/3 out (or the 2/3 for a hemisphere).

SQUARED_NOT_CUBED.student: A sphere uses the radius three times: r × r × r.
SQUARED_NOT_CUBED.teacher: Squares the radius where the formula cubes it.

HEMI_FORMULA.student: A whole sphere is (4/3) × π × r × r × r. Half of it is (2/3).
HEMI_FORMULA.teacher: Uses the half-sphere formula for a whole sphere.

WHOLE_FOR_HALF.student: A hemisphere is half a sphere. Halve the sphere's volume.
WHOLE_FOR_HALF.teacher: Gives the whole sphere for a hemisphere.

NO_TWO_THIRDS.student: A hemisphere is (2/3) × π × r × r × r. Keep the 2/3.
NO_TWO_THIRDS.teacher: Leaves the 2/3 out of the hemisphere formula.

FORGOT_SQUARE.student: Volume is π × r × r × h. Divide by r × r, not just r.
FORGOT_SQUARE.teacher: Divides by r once instead of r × r.

RADIUS_AS_DIAMETER.student: The radius is the number given. Do not halve it again.
RADIUS_AS_DIAMETER.teacher: Treats the given radius as a diameter and halves it.

STOPPED_AT_SQUARE.student: You found r × r. What number times itself gives that?
STOPPED_AT_SQUARE.teacher: Stops at r × r and does not take the square root.

DIAMETER_FOR_RADIUS.student: That is the diameter. The radius is half of it.
DIAMETER_FOR_RADIUS.teacher: Answers with the diameter where the radius is asked.

RADIUS_FOR_HEIGHT.student: That is the radius you were given. Divide the volume by r × r.
RADIUS_FOR_HEIGHT.teacher: Gives back the radius where the height is asked.

HEIGHT_FOR_RADIUS.student: That is the height you were given. Find r from r × r.
HEIGHT_FOR_RADIUS.teacher: Gives back the height where the radius is asked.

FORGOT_THIRD.student: A cone has the 1/3: V = (1/3) × π × r × r × h. Use it.

DIVIDED_NOT_MULTIPLIED.student: Undo the 1/3 by multiplying by 3, not dividing.
DIVIDED_NOT_MULTIPLIED.teacher: Divides by 3 where undoing the 1/3 needs × 3.

STOPPED_AT_CUBE.student: You found r × r × r. Which number cubed gives that?
STOPPED_AT_CUBE.teacher: Stops at r × r × r and does not take the cube root.

DIVIDED_NOT_ROOTED.student: A cube root is not ÷ 3. Which number times itself 3 times?
DIVIDED_NOT_ROOTED.teacher: Divides by 3 instead of taking the cube root.

COEFFICIENT_AS_RADIUS.student: That is the volume's number, not the radius. Undo the formula.
COEFFICIENT_AS_RADIUS.teacher: Reads the volume's coefficient as the radius.

RADIUS_FOR_DIAMETER.student: The diameter is twice the radius: all the way across.
RADIUS_FOR_DIAMETER.teacher: Answers with the radius where the diameter is asked.

LEFT_OUT_PI.student: Using 3 for π, put the 3 in where π would go.
LEFT_OUT_PI.teacher: Leaves out the 3 that replaces π.

LINEAR_SCALE.student: Count how many times that length is in the formula.
LINEAR_SCALE.teacher: Scales the volume by the plain factor, ignoring repeats.

SQUARE_FOR_CUBE.student: A sphere's radius appears three times: use the factor 3 times.
SQUARE_FOR_CUBE.teacher: Squares the scale factor where it should be cubed.

CUBE_FOR_SQUARE.student: The radius appears twice (r × r): use the factor twice.
CUBE_FOR_SQUARE.teacher: Cubes the scale factor where it should be squared.

SQUARE_FOR_LINEAR.student: Height appears once, so volume scales by just the factor.
SQUARE_FOR_LINEAR.teacher: Squares the factor for a length used once.

CUBE_FOR_LINEAR.student: Height appears once, so volume scales by just the factor.
CUBE_FOR_LINEAR.teacher: Cubes the factor for a length used once.

MULT_BY_EXPONENT.teacher: Multiplies the factor by the count instead of repeating it.

SPHERE_FOR_CONE.student: A ball is 2/3 of its can. The cone is 1/3.
SPHERE_FOR_CONE.teacher: Gives the ball's share for the cone.

CONE_FOR_SPHERE.student: The cone is 1/3 of the can. The ball is 2/3.
CONE_FOR_SPHERE.teacher: Gives the cone's share for the ball.

HALF_RULE.student: Neither is half: a cone is 1/3 and a ball 2/3 of the can.
